title: Me: You can now run DLSS 5 on AMD GPUs. My RX 9070 XT: Please stop, it hurts us
summary: A new app allows you to inject DLSS Neural Rendering deep into games even if you're running an AMD card. You probably won't want to, though.
body: Another day, another DLSS 5 story that actually kinda doesn't involve Nvidia itself doing anything, because it seems now AMD GPU owners can get in on the act. A new homebrew app has been released on Github that will allow you to run the DLSS Neural Rendering feature on a Radeon GPU. I've tried it and it works, but damn does it hurt the poor Radeon silicon. From having DLSS 5 .dll files plucked from an early access version of NBA 2K27, we've had modders working hard to create surprisingly polished ways to essentially get the tech working in practically any game , even if it doesn't natively support traditional DLSS itself. I've been playing around with it a lot this past week, even to the point of jamming it into Football Manager 26 just to see what would happen. And, y'know what, I kinda like the result so I'm keeping it. I wasn't expecting that, and I also wasn't expecting this technology, created by Nvidia, to appear so quickly on AMD GPUs. Historically we've found that where Nvidia goes, so AMD follows, at least in the GPU feature space, but it seems like AMD might not actually have to do much this time. Well, apart from actually make the silicon a little more tensor-friendly. …

title: D&D is getting a Netflix series about Strahd, involving the director of The Prisoner of Azkaban, and I honestly think this could work great
summary: I've been hankering after a Curse of Strahd adaptation for a long time.
body: Curse of Strahd is one of the most popular D&D modules for a reason—it's actually really compelling. Set in the misty, cursed lands of Barovia, Curse of Strahd is dominated by the titular Strahd von Zarovich, a vampire lord with a tragic backstory and a propensity for showing up at random intervals to give you a fantasy wedgie. In the one Strahd campaign I played in, my first encounter with the man involved him bleeding our cleric and making my thief drink his blood—so, you know. Normal. Anyway, per Deadline , we'll be getting a fully-fledged live action Netflix series about him dubbed Ravenloft—after the wider set of domains that darklords like Mr. Zarovich himself enjoy dominion over. It's being helmed by writer and executive producer John August and executive producer Alfonso Cuarón. The latter of which worked on Harry Potter: The Prisoner of Azkaban. Fittingly, one of the darker Harry Potter films—and owner of exactly the kind of murky, grey aesthetic I'd anticipate in any series taking place in Ravenloft. title: Sick of grinding for upgrade materials like leather and iron in Onimusha: Way of the Sword? Good news: you can buy a lot of them
summary: With the souls you get from killing Genma, not cash money.
body: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is the latest victim of the dreaded AAA videogame disease: Padded Runtime Via Unsatisfying Upgrade Materials . It could be a lot worse: thankfully there's no level gating in Onimusha that requires you to accrue an arbitrary set of stats before you can tackle a particular quest. It's not an RPG, and I'm sure as soon as Twitch streamers get their hands on it they'll be flexing on the hardest bosses without ever upgrading their gear by a single percentage point. But for us mortals, Onimusha's runtime is padded out by a pretty boring hub world full of pretty boring upgrade materials like cotton and iron that you use to very, very slowly increase your damage, health, stamina, and Oni power gauge. It's a dull system that doesn't evolve a single bit over the entire game. There are also rarer upgrade materials that you use to unlock abilities and enhancements on the skill tree. This structure encourages you to spend quite a few hours playing the least fun bits of Onimusha, but I do have some good news: there's a way to bypass some of the tedium that you can easily overlook. title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's mods immediately scrap the time pressure mechanic, which is apparently a dealbreaker for some people
summary: That didn't take much time.
body: The Blood of Dawnwalker 's out now—which means that players are getting introduced to its slightly more experimental take on RPG time. For the uninitiated, protagonist Coen has about 30 days and nights to save his family, the ticking clock of which is tracked in the UI. Completing quests, levelling up, and ticking off side-objectives costs "time segments". The idea, then, is to make it so that players have to (quite literally) spend their time wisely. In practice, this system doesn't have much in the way of actual teeth, acting more as a means to dissuade you from going all completionist on the map. In my playthrough, I've currently killed two out of three of Brencis' lieutenants and I still have 20 comfortable days and nights to spare. Which is probably why some folks have decided to opt out entirely. The " Better Story Timer " on Nexus Mods has options to triple the already-generous 30 day limit to 90 days, makes it so that perks and skills don't cost any time to obtain, and increases the number of segments in a day from eight to a whopping 32. This essentially means Coen can take his sweet time, pun intended, moseying around the Vale Sangora without a care in the world while hi…

title: Petit Planet's delightfully cosy galactic take on Animal Crossing is the closest we'll ever get to the life sim on PC
summary: Everyone's favourite cosy sim, now with gacha.
body: I had a lot of one-hour appointments at Gamescom, but none of them had time escaping from me quite like my 60 minutes with Petit Planet. It's Hoyoverse's attempt to tap into the Animal Crossing demographic, and by that I mean the developer has essentially taken Nintendo's cosy life sim and shot it up into space. I was honestly flabbergasted at how brazen the whole thing was. From the text boxes, to the character animations, to the little audio jingles that accompany them—near enough everything (bar its cosmic setting) screams Animal Crossing. But you know what? I kinda loved it. (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Like I mentioned, Petit Planet transports the cosy vibes traditionally reserved for land and sea and instead puts them in galactic pastures. That doesn't mean I'm locked out of biomes found on terra firma, though. After making my human character and being greeted by a delightfully pink bunny, I'm given two planets to pick from—one that's more your traditional forest-y vibes, and one that's significantly more desert-like. I picked the former, of course—though it looks like you might have even more starter options in the future—and set to work on building up a little planet of my ow…

It makes mainstream projectors look positively pedestrian. That's not to say it's perfect. There are a few niggles that take the triple-laser shine off this $5,000 beast, especially for gaming. But Xgimi's new big-screen beamer is an absolute stunner and deeply, deeply desirable. The basics begin with triple-laser RGB technology that's good for an eye-popping 7,000 lumens. That's combined, inevitably, with DLP and pixel-shift tech to deliver full 4K resolution at 60 Hz, plus 1080p at up to 240 Hz. Running at the latter setting, Xgimi claims that the Titan Noir Max is good for just 1 ms of latency. summary: Initial reports of a Nexon-developed shooter were met with doubt, but now something funky is happening with the StarCraft 2 website. And have you seen the BlizzCon schedule?
body: I don't want to get anybody's hopes up, but with BlizzCon 2026 now just over a week away, it really is starting to look like something—possibly something big —is happening in the world of StarCraft. The excitement began earlier this week when Korea's Chosun ( Google translated , via WCCFTech ) ran a story saying Nexon is close to finalizing a deal to develop a new game based on the StarCraft series. As Chosun noted, the series has been dormant since StarCraft Remastered in 2017; the last original StarCraft game, StarCraft 2, arrived all the way back in 2010. Despite that, the series remains hugely popular in Korea. The StarCraft subreddit took some issues with the report: For one thing, Chosun suggested the new game would be StarCraft 3, rather than the StarCraft shooter Nexon is reportedly working on . Still, the timing seemed right: BlizzCon 2026 runs September 12-13, which is now less than two weeks away. title: A multi-month delay for Deus Ex turned into a huge payoff for one of its best characters, says designer Harvey Smith
summary: Smith's story about the late stages of Deus Ex development takes some time to get to the point, but it's a fun ride.
body: Nobody likes game delays. Sure, a delay is temporary and suck is forever , as Gabe Newell once said, but it still chafes. But sometimes a little extra development time can go a very long way. In a new interview with the NoClip podcast , immersive sim maestro Harvey Smith shared one such story about Deus Ex, explaining how it leveraged some extra post-production time to give a much bigger role to one of the game's most famous NPCs—and make it a much better game in the process. Smith's tale actually followed a remark by Ben Horne, his co-founder at the new Black Pony Immersive studio, who said, "You can elevate a good immersive sim into a great immersive sim in a very short amount of time, a matter of months, if you just protect a post-production time." Publishers generally don't want to hear that, Smith added—although he obviously agrees with the sentiment—and so 20-some years ago, when Ion Storm Austin asked Eidos for more time to tighten up Deus Ex, "We geared up for this giant fight." Instead, Eidos just said yes. "They were so distracted by what was happening in Dallas with Daikatana and such that they were like, 'Sure, sure, sure. Take five more months, take six more, whatever…

title: The bizarre spirit of classic Elder Scrolls games is alive and well in little lo-fi RPG A Short Quest
summary: A few hours with a recent playtest has me eager to play the full thing next year.
body: When a big old tree talks, I listen. He said, "I have a task of great importance," as soon as I opened my eyes, and who was I to turn him down? "Take this note to the King, it should be a short quest," he instructed, and although there is no king in the playtest for A Short Quest , I am eager to fulfill the tree's wishes when the whole game is out next year. There are actually a lot of mysterious things I found in the few hours I spent with A Short Quest that I'd like to know more about. Every time I passed by a pond it spoke and asked me to dance (jump three times) for a blueberry. I found a note in an old mine that told me how to find the "glyph cipher" on the side of a cart, but I still don't know what to do with it. And I'm still not sure why I was summoned into the underground domain of a ghost wizard who tried to kill me. A Short Quest reminded me of when I would watch a friend from middle school play Morrowind on his Xbox or when I played Oblivion for the first time. It's a lo-fi first-person RPG that's trying to evoke that earlier, goofier era of the form; back when an elf would fall out of the sky and drop a scroll of flight as a joke. title: Guild Wars 3 is a lot smaller scale than Guild Wars 2 because of the new approach to combat and movement: 'You would probably see about 20 players in a large combat scenario'
summary: Expect more clarity, but no more 100-player boss fights.
body: At Gamescom, I got to see a hands-off demo of Guild Wars 3 and chatted to the developers about what they have in store for us when the MMO hits beta next year. You can read about the significant changes to movement and combat in my Guild Wars 3 preview , but we also discussed how different the upcoming MMO's scale will be when compared to its predecessors. Guild Wars 3 sits between OG Guild Wars, which was very small scale, and Guild Wars 2, where you could fight a boss with a hundred other players. It still has that multiplayer focus, but compared to Guild Wars 2, ArenaNet has significantly reduced how many people you'll be playing with at once. "At most, out in the open world, you would probably see about 20 players in a large combat scenario," says game director Colin Johanson. "Our movement systems and our combat systems, in particular, are really high fidelity. They're designed to lend themselves to being able to see everything that's going on, and we felt like that number is where it starts to cap out. You start losing some of the visceral sense of what the gameplay is like." Johnason adds that, at the high end of player numbers, the action starts to become "more spectacle t…

title: Zach Cregger doesn't want to get bogged down in 'the wild aspects' of Resident Evil's lore: 'I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat'
summary: The trench coat is actually integral to the build.
body: What's the weirdest bit of Resident Evil lore you know of? Is it the fact that Claire Redfield's favourite food is a cheeseburger? Maybe it's that Hunk spent a week lost in Raccoon City's sewers eating rats after getting his ass beaten by Birkin? Or perhaps it's that the Tyrant's trench coat is more than just a bold fashion statement—it's actually integral to the build. There's been a few explanations as to why Tyrants wear trench coats in Resident Evil games. One perk of the coat is that it helps disguise the mutations, which allows Tyrants to infiltrate more sensitive areas, but its biggest bonus is its power-limiting function. Wearing the trench coat holds the Tyrant together by preventing out-of-control mutations, and if it's damaged or the Tyrant removes it you'll get a Super Tyrant. (Image credit: Capcom) You'd be forgiven for not knowing this as it's not exactly a widely talked about tidbit, which is exactly why Zach Cregger, director of the upcoming Resident Evil movie, is staying away from Resident Evil's deep lore: to keep the film as grounded as possible. title: Both Microsoft and Sony say they're under no obligation to pass tariff refunds on to customers
summary: One for me, none for thee.
body: Tech tariffs imposed by the Trump administration were ruled unconstitutional back in February , though the saga is far from over. Many companies have since sought refunds, and consumers battling rising hardware prices are wondering whether they'll see those recouped costs trickle down. Well, as far as major players Microsoft and Sony are concerned, the answer is 'No.' To rewind a smidge, consoles have been climbing in price for some time now. An Xbox gamer filed a proposed class-action lawsuit against Microsoft back in July , accusing the company of passing on the cost of tariffs to consumers. A similar lawsuit was filed against Sony back in May . Now, lawyers from both companies are arguing that their respective sides are simply under no obligation to pass on tariff refunds to customers. As reported by Game File , Microsoft’s legal team filed a motion to dismiss its lawsuit last month, saying, "There is nothing unjust about Plaintiff purchasing an Xbox at an advertised price and getting exactly what he paid for—regardless of whatever theory he devised months later about Microsoft’s cost structure." title: PUBG's new spin-off game is 'faster, meaner, and more aggressive' with sword hands and 'a little bit of light cannibalism'
summary: "PUBG is deliberate and thoughtful and tactical. This is not that."
body: PUBG remains one of Steam's most-played games, which makes it all the more surprising that PUBG Studios and publisher Krafton haven't made more attempts to milk it over the years. PUBG: DED NET might be the biggest yank of the udder to date though, revealing an entirely new spin-off roguelite FPS set in the '90s. And if you didn't know the game was set in the '90s, you sure will after the game's trailer beats you over the head with period-accurate vibes. Creative director Dave Curd helpfully informs me that the "DED" in DED NET stands for "dog eat dog," which makes the words emblazoned across one of the miniguns in the trailer make a whole lot more sense. I've sat down with Curd in the hours after the game's reveal at Gamescom's Opening Night Live, where he tells me a little bit more about what players can expect from DED NET. Curd says DED NET is going to be "unhinged" and "unfiltered" with the promise of tons of build variety that'll unfurl the more matches you play. "Every run starts different, and you'll always have something in mind. Maybe this run I want to be the very close quartered, door kicker, riot shield guy. Maybe this run I want to be more of a trickster or prankster…

title: Guild Wars 3's approach to combat and movement is like nothing I've ever seen in an MMO before: 'One of our big goals when we make a new game in the Guild Wars franchise is to set out and try new things'
summary: Wall running, mantling, aerial attacks, multiplayer combos—it's a lot of new stuff.
body: There are few things as exciting as the prospect of a new MMO. And when that new MMO is from ArenaNet, the studio that's been focused on Guild Wars for more than two decades, the excitement is even greater. Having seen Guild Wars 3 in action at Gamescom, and spoken to game director Colin Johanson and lead combat designer Kevin Stocker, my excitement has been justified. Just as Guild Wars 2 was dramatically different from its predecessor, Guild Wars 3 is not a simple sequel. It's distinct from GW2, a very different kind of MMO, and one that even in the short space of time I spent watching it being played is full of novel ideas. (Image credit: ArenaNet) The first big change is in its setting. The clock has been turned back 1,000 years, and we're heading to Orr—a land that in GW2's era is a post-apocalyptic hellscape, but at this earlier point is a verdant wilderness teeming with spirits. "The origins of the Guild Wars franchise originate out of Orr," says Johanson. "This is a time before the gods have left the world, very shortly after Grenth has usurped Dhuum and become the god of death. This is a time where the first guilds are starting to rise across the world, and before the ver…

title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword has a hard mode, but it isn't unlocked from the start
summary: Here are the difficulty options you can change to make Onimusha harder.
body: Some players came away from Onimusha's demo worried that the game would be too easy, a concern I've addressed in-depth based on my own time with the game. The good news is that I think the challenge level is well-judged for most people, and Onimusha does have a hard mode. For those who hoped to jump right into the hardest possible difficulty from the main menu, though, I've got some bad news: you're going to have to beat the game first. Onimusha: Way of the Sword's default difficulty options Story : "A difficulty level that lets you focus on the story. Recommended for action game beginners." Musashi deals more damage and stamina damage and takes less from enemy attacks Action prompts default to on, showing button icons for how to deal with incoming enemy attacks Action : "A difficulty level for those who like challenging battles. This difficulty level will keep you on your toes. Recommended for experienced action game players." You can freely change between these two options from save points throughout the game. title: Acer's bizarre hybrid handheld/laptop concept is way more interesting than what is actually getting released this year
summary: Flippin' 'eck.
body: While I've bemoaned the expensive state of handheld gaming PCs at length , that doesn't mean I find a cool concept model any less head-turning. Enter Acer's latest Project DualPlay creation: a handheld gaming PC with a flippable screen that can turn into a laptop. The Project DualPlay Mini was shown off on-stage at IFA 2026, in Berlin . It's all about reimagining "what a gaming handheld form factor can do," exploring a design that functions "both as a gaming handheld and as a mobile productivity station," according to Acer . As a concept machine, however, the Project DualPlay Mini might not see the light of day beyond the IFA stage. What will see a wide release later this year, though, is the Acer Predator Atlas 7. Very simply, this is a cut-down version of Acer's chunkier Predator Atlas 8 handheld . For starters, the seven-inch touchscreen still enjoys a 120 Hz refresh rate and 500 nits of peak brightness. The device also has an 80Whr battery, and the guts of this new seven-inch form factor still includes Intel Arc B390 graphics, and an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor. In other words, it's got all of the power, but less of the heft. It will be available in winter 2026, though the …

body: Picture this: I am emerging from a pile of paper, red string, and thumbtacks, hair (I have hair in this scenario) dishevelled, breathless, yelling like I've well and truly lost it: I knew it! title: Gigabyte GO27Q24A Review
summary: An affordable QD-OLED gaming monitor that’s got it where it counts.
body: We’ve been reviewing some silly-priced gaming monitors in recent times but, some of the latest-and-greatest models wield premium features that are unnecessary for many buyers. Gigabyte’s GO27Q24A strives to keep things simple by stripping-away some of the less-universally popular, expensive technologies to produce a spartan gaming monitor that focuses on the category’s most-important facets, to keep the price down. Gigabyte has successfully done this before using WOLED and Tandem OLED panels in the same range, so how will this QD-OLED model fare? Assembling the Gigabyte GO27Q24A is simple: the stem clips to the screen and the stand uses a single thumbscrew to attach to the stem without any tools being needed. The stand is the same, solid, small-footprint unit that Gigabyte’s premium monitors use and it lets competitive types sit right up close to the screen. The stem is also the same seen on its superior siblings and affords a generous degree of manipulation to get the screen sitting just so: there’s -5°~+21° tilt, ±15° swivel and 90° pivot. There’s also 13 cm of height adjustment. Impressive. Gigabyte GO27Q24A specs Screen size 27-inch Resolution 2560 x 1440 Brightness 200 nits f…

title: CD Projekt mystery games update: Yes, they're still happening, and no, not any time soon
summary: Maybe someday we'll find out what's going on with Sirius and Hadar, but it is not this day.
body: CD Projekt has a lot going on these days: The Witcher 4 , Cyberpunk 2 , a new Witcher 3 expansion and remaster , a remake of the original Witcher , probably some other stuff I've either forgotten or don't know about, and a couple of long-simmering mystery projects that are still only known by their codenames, Sirius and Hadar. You'd be forgiven for forgetting about them, given their low profile and drawn-out development times, but in today's H1 investors call , CD Projekt's vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnaś reassured everyone that they're still happening—just not anytime soon. Asked about Sirius, Gnaś mentioned the recent cuts to the development team , saying—as CD Projekt did when the layoffs happened—that the changes were made to meet "the current needs of the project." "Pre-production is ongoing, and at this stage we are focused on testing different solutions and ideas we develop," Gnaś said. "This project is very different from our other projects because it's focused on multiplayer. So there's a lot of learning and testing in this particular one." title: How to sell silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: The Vrakhiri's reign makes it hard to find a merchant buying silver.
body: I had no trouble finding vendors to offload Coen's endless supply of low-value pilfered junk in Blood of Dawnwalker , but it took a few days to figure out how to sell silver . It makes sense that silver is considered contraband under vampire rule, so you have to find the right vendor to foist it on and complete a quick quest before adventuring south. Where can you sell silver in Blood of Dawnwalker? (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) You can sell silver in Svartrau City to the aptly named Silver Trader, but before you leave Coen's home in Laslea Glen, complete the Into the Den quest. It doesn't take long to slay the ravenous bear, and you need the intel uncovered by investigating what remains of its dinner. Any item with a white chalice icon is silver contraband Complete Into the Den, a quest that begins east of the Northern Foothill Head south to Svatrau City and speak with the Silver Trader Tell him you know he's dealing in silver, and he'll agree to trade In the name of RPG science, I tried heading to Svartrau immediately and skipping Into the Den, but the Silver Trader just tells Coen to get lost. You've gotta kill the bear, sorry. A note at the end of the quest points Coen to Svart…

title: Full prologue walkthrough and quest order for The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Use this ideal quest order to get the least bloody mass because there's not enough time to do it all and lives are on the line.
body: How time works Time-sensitive quests are marked with a clock 🕑 in your quest log. There are eight time segments each day (and eight each night). Quests that use up time have an hourglass symbol ⏳ and number to indicate how many segments they use. ⚠️ Getting caught stealing will waste four time segments with the guard. ⚠️ Be careful about learning skills at shrines during the prologue; some use up time to unlock. Full prologue walkthrough Your first choice in the prologue is whether Coen should force-feed his mother Esme at his father Pieter's direction. TL;DR: this choice doesn't have any long term impact but after that you'll need to start managing your time as the prologue begins in earnest. title: All Witchcraft ability manual locations in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Learn these hexes to confound your enemies.
body: Finding Witchcraft manuals really helps make Blood of Dawnwalker 's human combat a lot of fun. These hexes can summon a murder of crows, set enemy blood ablaze, or even protect and reflect against a single instance of damage. The catch, however, is that you'll have to track down skill manuals to unlock them. I'll run through where to find them all below and provide a list of all the Witchcraft vendors you can buy manuals from. All Witchcraft ability locations There are ten Witchcraft abilities, but you'll unlock Compel Soul, Astral Communion, Burning Blood, and Mercurial Fervour from Anca towards the end of the prologue. You'll have to find manuals to unlock the other six and level them all, which you can usually get via completing Ancient Circles, Haunted Sites, or any of the Pilgrimage of Power quests. You can also find them in bookcases, or purchase them from any of the following Witchcraft merchants: Merchant Location Anca You unlock her as a vendor at the Crossroads Inn in St. Tyna's Grove after you complete Echoes of Silenced Bells .
